arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ford's counsel argued that specific jurisdiction requires suit-related conduct in the forum state. He stated that the defendant must engage in conduct relevant to the claims.
Justice Breyer noted that the doctrine aims to prevent unfairness to defendants. He observed that the car was sent to the state.
Justice Thomas questioned the connection between the Due Process Clause and proximate cause. He asked counsel to trace the legal lineage of this requirement.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if advertising in all states satisfies jurisdictional requirements. He posed a hypothetical about a safety claim arising from an ad.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Ford argues that specific jurisdiction requires suit-related conduct in the forum state. The company claims its advertising does not satisfy this requirement.
Montana argues that the Due Process Clause allows jurisdiction based on relatedness. The state claims the car sale connects to the injury.
